name: Sprocket
text: We should implement A/B testing for the new feature with 5% of users. This decision allows us to gather data on user interaction and performance, providing insights into the feature's effectiveness. The trade-off is that it may delay the full rollout, but the data-driven approach will minimize risks and ensure that we prioritize quality and user experience.

name: Gauge
text: A/B testing with only 5% of users risks missing critical insights because it doesn’t capture the full range of user interactions, which could lead to misleading conclusions. A better alternative is to perform a visible A/B test that includes a larger cohort, ensuring broader data collection and reducing the risk of self-selection bias. To settle this argument, we should analyze past A/B test results to see how smaller cohorts affected decision-making and whether they led to significant insights or missed opportunities.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do a 10% blind rollout to users who opted into the new feature. This gives us enough data to spot major issues without skewing metrics with a visible banner. The trade-off is that 10% is still small enough to miss edge cases affecting the remaining 90%, but it’s the fastest way to validate core stability before expanding.

name: Gauge
text: A 10% blind rollout to users who opted in can introduce self-selection bias, meaning the data may not represent the entire user base accurately. A better alternative is to conduct a visible A/B test with at least 30% of users, which would ensure a more inclusive set of feedback and minimize the chances of missing edge cases or issues that only affect specific segments. To settle this, we could examine past data from similar rollouts to determine the optimal test group size that provided actionable insights without skewing results.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Implement a hybrid 5% pilot with a 3% visible A/B test and a 2% blind rollout to a truly randomized set of users, which will deliver a dataset that balances the need for statistical significance with the risk of introducing bias, and the lead will own the resulting artifact, ensuring it meets quality standards before full rollout.
